title: The AI race built faster chips. Now the chips are too fast for their own wires.
excerpt: For three years, the AI race has been a race for faster chips. Eliyan just became a $1bn company by pointing out that the chips are now too fast for their own wires. content_html:
For three years, the AI race has been a race for faster chips. Eliyan just became a $1bn company by pointing out that the chips are now too fast for their own wires.

The Santa Clara startup said it closed an oversubscribed $145m Series C at a $1bn valuation, making it a unicorn, the company announced. Seligman Ventures led the round. Two strategic investors joined, Cisco Investments and Lumentum.

The bottleneck moved

Modern AI accelerators can crunch numbers far faster than they can be fed. So they sit idle, waiting for data. Eliyan’s chief executive Ramin Farjadrad put a number on it to Reuters: “Today we are at the point that we are maybe 30-40% of the GPUs is being used, and is being mainly limited by how fast they can receive the data to process. We’re solving that problem.”

Eliyan sells the plumbing, not the compute. Its NuLink links and NuGear chiplets shuttle data between chips, between packages, and across racks. The pitch is simple. Faster, lower-power connections let a data centre’s expensive silicon run closer to full tilt.

The biggest players already solved this in-house. Nvidia bought the networking firm Mellanox for $6.8bn in 2019, and has since turned that into its own interconnect lock-in. Google and Amazon lean on Broadcom and Marvell instead.

Eliyan wants to be the neutral option, licensing its technology and selling chiplets to anyone building their own AI chips. That is why its share register reads like a customer list. Earlier rounds drew AMD, Arm, Meta, Intel, Micron, Samsung and SK hynix. The new money adds Cisco and Lumentum, both from the optical world.

From electrical to optical

The two new backers point to where Eliyan is heading. It made its name in electrical links between dies, using standard packaging rather than pricier silicon interposers. Now it is pushing into optical interconnects, the light-based links that hyperscalers increasingly need to move data between racks without burning huge amounts of power.

The founders framed the raise as a bet on a deeper shift. “AI infrastructure is undergoing one of the largest architectural transitions in computing history,” Farjadrad said. “As compute, memory, packaging, and networking become increasingly interconnected, traditional approaches to system connectivity are reaching their limits. Eliyan was founded to address these challenges at the architectural level.”

What the money buys

The cash will fund development, ecosystem partnerships and manufacturing. Eliyan expects to start shipping chiplets this year, and told Reuters it forecasts hundreds of millions of dollars in sales by the end of 2027, up from “low millions” in 2025. It holds more than 100 patents.

Investors are paying up for the unglamorous part of the stack. Umesh Padval of Seligman Ventures, who sat on Mellanox’s board when Nvidia bought it, is joining Eliyan’s board. He argues the connections now decide the winners.

“As AI systems continue to scale, efficient electrical and optical interconnects that enable future scale-up and scale-out networks between compute and memory are becoming the performance-defining technologies of modern AI data centers. Eliyan has developed a differentiated architecture to address this challenge, combining deep semiconductor expertise and a scalable approach to the evolving needs of next-generation AI systems.”

He is not alone in the bet. In March, the optical-interconnect startup Ayar Labs raised $500m at a $3.75bn valuation. The memory and chip suppliers now on Eliyan’s cap table have a direct stake in the same idea. As AI systems grow from single chips into rack-sized machines, the wires between the chips may command as much attention as the chips themselves.

三年来，人工智能竞赛一直是一场速度更快的芯片的竞赛。 Eliyan 刚刚成为一家价值 10 亿美元的公司，因为他指出现在的芯片速度对于他们自己的线路来说太快了。

该公司宣布，这家圣克拉拉初创公司表示，它以 10 亿美元的估值完成了超额认购的 1.45 亿美元 C 轮融资，使其成为独角兽。 Seligman Ventures 领投此轮融资。 思科投资公司和 Lumentum 两家战略投资者加入。

瓶颈转移了

现代人工智能加速器处理数字的速度远远快于输入数据的速度。 所以他们闲着，等待数据。 Eliyan 的首席执行官 Ramin Farjadrad 向路透社透露了一个数字：“目前，我们可能使用了 30-40% 的 GPU，并且主要受到它们接收数据处理速度的限制。 我们正在解决这个问题。”

Eliyan 销售管道，而不是计算机。 其 NuLink 链路和 NuGear 小芯片可在芯片之间、封装之间以及跨机架传输数据。 球场很简单。 更快、更低功耗的连接让数据中心昂贵的芯片更接近全速运行。

巨头的独立替代品

最大的参与者已经在内部解决了这个问题。 Nvidia 于 2019 年以 68 亿美元收购了网络公司 Mellanox，此后将其转变为自己的互连锁定。 谷歌和亚马逊则依赖博通和 Marvell。

Eliyan 希望成为中立的选择，向任何构建自己的人工智能芯片的人授权其技术并向任何人出售小芯片。 这就是为什么它的股份登记册读起来就像一份客户名单。 早期轮次吸引了 AMD、Arm、Meta、英特尔、美光、三星和 SK 海力士。 新资金增加了来自光学领域的 Cisco 和 Lumentum。

从电到光

两位新的支持者指出了埃利扬的前进方向。 它因芯片之间的电气连接而闻名，使用标准封装而不是昂贵的硅中介层。 现在，它正在推进光学互连，超大规模企业越来越需要这种基于光的链路来在机架之间移动数据，而无需消耗大量电力。

创始人将此次加薪视为对更深层次转变的押注。 Farjadrad 表示：“人工智能基础设施正在经历计算历史上最大的架构转变之一。” “随着计算、内存、封装和网络的互联程度越来越高，传统的系统连接方法已经达到了极限。 Eliyan 的成立就是为了在架构层面解决这些挑战。”

钱买什么

这笔现金将用于资助开发、生态系统合作伙伴关系和制造。 Eliyan 预计今年开始出货小芯片，并告诉路透社，预计到 2027 年底销售额将达到数亿美元，高于 2025 年的“数百万美元”。 拥有100多项专利。

投资者正在为该堆栈中乏味的部分付出代价。 Seligman Ventures 的 Umesh Padval 即将加入 Eliyan 的董事会，他在 Nvidia 收购 Mellanox 时担任该公司的董事会成员。 他认为现在关系决定了胜利者。

“随着人工智能系统不断扩展，高效的电气和光学互连正在成为现代人工智能数据中心的性能定义技术，这些互连能够实现未来计算和内存之间的纵向扩展和横向扩展网络。 Eliyan 开发了一种差异化架构来应对这一挑战，结合深厚的半导体专业知识和可扩展的方法来满足下一代人工智能系统不断变化的需求。”

他并不是唯一一个打赌的人。 3 月份，光互连初创公司 Ayar Labs 筹集了 5 亿美元资金，估值为 37.5 亿美元。 现在 Eliyan 资本表上的内存和芯片供应商与同样的想法有着直接的利害关系。 随着人工智能系统从单芯片发展为机架大小的机器，芯片之间的电线可能会像芯片本身一样受到关注。
